result.summary: Lens 4 verdict: the document's code anchors are unusually accurate. Seven of the eight cited locations point at exactly the code claimed, in the current tree, with no line drift - repack.cpp:4889, 4456-4469, 51; arch/riscv/quants.c:32; ggml-cpu.c:257; and build.sh really does set -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF for every variant. All 48 published 27B cycle figures match the logs byte-for-byte and `bash sweep.sh --md` regenerates the tables. Two mechanistic claims do not survive: (a) the "vector twin gated behind __riscv_zvfh" does not exist on RISC-V at all - arch-fallback.h:221 aliases the generic scalar routine to the arch name, so both arms of the #if at repack.cpp:347 call the same scalar function and flipping GGML_RV_ZVFH=ON would change nothing; (b) the M-tile-sharing citation arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972 lives inside the `Q1_VD4DOT` block, i.e. the d4 build, yet it is cited to explain a `+repack` measurement (the mechanism is nonetheless real in the baseline kernel at lines 2120-2132). Separately, the central causal story - that F is the scalar activation quantizer - was never measured directly, only curve-fitted; I built an independent cross-check the document does not perform (fit F on the seven 27B ne0=5120 nodes: F doubles from ~450K to ~880K exactly as ne0 doubles 2560->5120), which corroborates it, but the 6-significant-figure F=489,581 rests on a fit with +/-5.2% residuals whose two-point estimates span 407K-690K, and the derived superlative "bigger than the kernel it feeds" flips depending on which pair you fit.

verified_ok.claim: 'The dispatch gate at `repack.cpp:4889` requires `cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0`' - the line number and the condition.
verified_ok.evidence: `grep -n 'ne\[1\] % 64' ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp` -> line 4889 exactly: `if (__riscv_vlenb() * 8 >= 512 && cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0 && cur->ne[0] % QK1_0 == 0) {`. No line drift; the quoted condition is really there, inside `else if (cur->type == GGML_TYPE_Q1_0)` (4885) and `if (ggml_cpu_has_riscv_v())` (4886).

verified_ok.claim: ssm_alpha / ssm_beta (48 rows) are the only measured tensors the gate rejects, and every build therefore runs the stock kernel on them.
verified_ok.evidence: 48 % 64 != 0. Every other measured ne1 (10240, 6144, 5120, 17408, 12288, 1024, 4096, 9728, 2560) is a multiple of 64. The four 27B builds land at 936,969 / 939,289 / 939,798 / 938,688 (sweep-gemm-27b/{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}-k49.log), spread 0.30% - matches the document's '0.3%'.

verified_ok.claim: 'the gemm loads each weight vector once and fires four dots against it' - the mechanism itself.
verified_ok.evidence: arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1968 loads one sign mask `__riscv_vlm_v_b4(...)`, 1969 builds one weight vector `w`, 1970-1971 passes that single `w` to `q1_vd4dots_4acc_m2` with four activation words. The same shape holds in the NON-vd4dot gemm actually used at `+repack`: line 2121 loads `sign` once, lines 2124-2131 accumulate four independent sums from it.

verified_ok.claim: 'while the gemv reloads it per token'.
verified_ok.evidence: repack.cpp:4406-4409: `for (int iter = nrows - (nrows % 4); iter < nrows; iter++) { gemv<...>(..., 1 /* nrows */, ncols); }` - one whole gemv call, and therefore one whole weight pass, per leftover token.

verified_ok.claim: '`forward_mul_mat` quantizes activations before the kernel runs (`repack.cpp:4456-4469`)' and the 4-token vs non-multiple-of-4 dispatch.
verified_ok.evidence: repack.cpp:4456-4469 read verbatim. 4460: `for (int64_t i11 = ith * 4; i11 < ne11 - ne11 % 4; i11 += nth * 4)` calling `ggml_quantize_mat_t<INTER_SIZE, PARAM_TYPE>(..., 4, ne10)`; 4465-4468: `const int64_t i11_processed = ne11 - ne11 % 4; for (...) from_float(...)`. With ne11=4 only the first loop runs; with ne11=2 only the second. INTER_SIZE=1 / PARAM_TYPE=Q8_0 confirmed from the traits instance at repack.cpp:4734 `tensor_traits<block_q1_0, 1, 64, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0> q1_0_64x1_q8_0`, so the document's `ggml_quantize_mat_t<1, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0>` is right.

verified_ok.claim: The measured gemm legs really did run with ne11 = 4 tokens (so the 4-token branch is the one taken).
verified_ok.evidence: ggml-cpu.c:1780-1782 prints `nrows=` from `tensor->src[1]->ne[1]`, i.e. ne11. All 48 sweep-gemm-27b logs carry `nrows=4`; sweep.sh's `read_leg` awk rejects any leg whose nrows disagrees with WANT_NROWS as BAD-NROWS.

verified_ok.claim: '`ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic` -- a **pure scalar** loop (`repack.cpp:51`, its own comment says `// scalar`): per 32-column block, 128 `fabsf` for the amax scan plus 128 `roundf`'.
verified_ok.evidence: repack.cpp:51 is the function; line 58 is `// scalar`. Outer loop 63 over nb = k/32 blocks; 64-70 is 4 rows x 32 columns = 128 `fabsf` (line 69); 78-85 is `for (int j = 0; j < QK8_0 * 4; j++)` = 128 iterations each ending in `y[i].qs[j] = roundf(x0)` (line 84). No vector intrinsic anywhere in the body.

verified_ok.claim: '`quantize_row_q8_0`, which **is** RVV-vectorized on RISC-V (`arch/riscv/quants.c:32`, gated only on `__riscv_v`)'.
verified_ok.evidence: arch/riscv/quants.c:32 is `void quantize_row_q8_0(...)`; the RVV body opens at line 39 with `#if defined(__riscv_v)` (vle32/vfabs/vfredmax/vfncvt at 45-64) and the `#else` at 66-70 falls back to `quantize_row_q8_0_ref`. No zvfh, zfh or vlen condition.

verified_ok.claim: '`.nrows = 1` (`ggml-cpu.c:257`) means one `vec_dot` per (weight row, token), so there is no prefill kernel upstream at all'.
verified_ok.evidence: ggml-cpu.c:253-258 is the `[GGML_TYPE_Q1_0]` entry with `.nrows = 1` on line 257 exactly. That field is read at 1300 into `vec_dot_num_rows`, copied to `num_rows_per_vec_dot` at 1463, and used as the token-loop stride at 1239 and the row-loop stride at 1268-1269, so each `vec_dot` covers one weight row and one token.

verified_ok.claim: 'the measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`'.
verified_ok.evidence: build.sh, function `cfg()`: `-DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`. cfg() is the single configure path for all six variants (pristine/baseline/prefetch/d4/d4-nopf/*-nodpref), so every leg carries it. ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt:483-484 confirms GGML_RV_ZVFH is what appends `_zvfh` to -march, i.e. what defines `__riscv_zvfh`.

verified_ok.claim: Every 27B cycle figure printed in the document is the number in the log.
verified_ok.evidence: Cross-checked all 48 `[andesim] N cycles` lines in sweep-gemm-27b/*.log against the four cycle columns of both layer tables - exact match on all 48. `MODEL=27b NODES="48 49 50 51 52 53 54 55" bash sweep.sh --md` (read-only path; the script exits before the `[ -f $GGUF ]` check and before xargs) reproduces layer 6 row-for-row and its 20.60x geomean; the layer-7 command reproduces the 4 measured rows.

verified_ok.claim: The whole F / T fit table ('| variant | gemm `F` | gemm `T` | gemv `F` | gemv `T` |') reproduces from the 4B logs.
verified_ok.evidence: Least-squares fit of cycles = F + T*(ne1/64) on the five 4B ne0=2560 nodes (attn_q/attn_v/attn_k/ffn_gate/ffn_up) from sweep-gemm/*.log and sweep-gemv/*.log reproduces all six published pairs to the digit: gemm baseline 398,003/80,915; gemm prefetch 441,355/76,544; gemm d4 489,581/23,036; gemv baseline 13,379/133,082; gemv prefetch 27,294/85,084; gemv d4 39,491/21,638. Derived figures also check: 489,581/39,491 = 12.40x ('12.4x'), 23,036/4 = 5,759, 21,638/2 = 10,819, ratio 1.879 ('1.88x'), F/attn_v = 59.5% ('59%'), F/ffn_gate = 12.3% ('12%').

verified_ok.claim: The document's causal mechanism (F is a per-activation-element cost, not a kernel cost) - corroborated by a test the document does not perform.
verified_ok.evidence: I fitted the same affine model on the seven 27B nodes that share ne0 = 5120 (attn_qkv, attn_gate, ffn_gate, ffn_up, attn_q, attn_v, attn_k) from sweep-gemm-27b/*.log: F = 824,191 (baseline) / 920,157 (prefetch) / 895,692 (d4) against 4B's 398,003 / 441,355 / 489,581 at ne0 = 2560. F scales ~2.0x with a 2.0x ne0 while T collapses - exactly what a per-element activation quantizer predicts and what a fixed per-node overhead would not.

verified_ok.claim: '**Upstream is exactly linear in tokens.** Measured on all 12 nodes: 1.97x to 2.01x for 2x the tokens.'
verified_ok.evidence: 27B pristine gemm (sweep-gemm-27b/pristine-k{48..59}.log) divided by the 27B pristine gemv column of profiling_gemv_27b.md, node by node: 1.985, 1.975, 1.992, 2.008, 1.972, 1.988, 1.992, 2.012, 2.002, 1.998, 1.996, 1.977. Range 1.972-2.012, which rounds to the published 1.97x-2.01x.

verified_ok.evidence: ffn_gate vs ffn_up upstream 309,587,645 vs 309,915,506 = 0.106% apart ('0.11%'); at d4 14,351,598 vs 14,349,546 = 0.014% ('0.01%'); ssm_out vs attn_output upstream 122,621,082 vs 119,759,239 = 2.39% ('2.4%'). All three from the logs.

findings.title: There is no RISC-V vector twin of the 4x1 activation quantizer; GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF is not what makes prefill scalar
findings.claim_in_doc:
Its vector twin is gated behind `__riscv_zvfh`, and the
  measurement build sets `-DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF`.
findings.what_i_checked: `grep -rn ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1 ggml/` returns exactly four hits: the declaration (repack.h:208), the alias (arch-fallback.h:221), the call (repack.cpp:348) and the definition of the *_generic* name (repack.cpp:51). Read repack.cpp:342-352, repack.cpp:12 (`#include "arch-fallback.h"`), and arch-fallback.h:216-256 (the `#elif defined(__riscv)` block, reached because the preceding branches at lines 7/76/88/118/167 are GGML_CPU_GENERIC/arm/x86/ppc/loongarch). Confirmed with `git log -L 342,352:ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp` (commit 8734bdb7e).
findings.finding: arch-fallback.h:221 unconditionally does `#define ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` on every RISC-V build - there is no zvfh guard on that alias, and no RISC-V implementation of the vector routine exists anywhere in the tree. After preprocessing, the scalar body at repack.cpp:51 IS `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1`, so both arms of the `#if defined(__riscv_zvfh) && defined(__riscv_v)` at repack.cpp:347-351 resolve to the same scalar function. Building with -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=ON would not give prefill a vector quantizer. The author's own opt_roadmap.md (F4d, line ~207) states this correctly - 'un-gated quantize_mat_t<1,Q8_0> from zvfh (generic 4x1 otherwise)' - and lists 'activation quantize RVV' as a remaining lever, i.e. as unwritten code.
findings.impact: No cycle number or speedup in either table changes - prefill genuinely does run a scalar quantizer, which is what the measurements reflect. What changes is the cause and the remedy: the document points a reader at a build flag ('the measurement build sets -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF'), implying the measurement handicapped itself and that flipping one CMake option recovers the loss. It does not. The real work is writing an RVV `ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1` for RISC-V, which is what the closing sentence ('Vectorizing it is the clearest remaining prefill win') actually implies. A third party auditing the build config would conclude the run was mis-configured and dismiss the result.

findings.title: Pristine never pays the scalar activation quantizer, so the 'before' and 'after' builds do not share the same activation path
findings.claim_in_doc:
`F` is not part of the kernel. ... It is the shared
activation path, and the source says what it is.
findings.what_i_checked: build.sh: `pristine` is configured `-DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`, so `ggml_backend_cpu_repack_buffer_type` is not registered and repack.cpp's `forward_mul_mat` (with its 4456-4469 quantize block) never runs. Read the upstream path instead: ggml-cpu.c:1280 `ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat`, line 1299-1300 `from_float = type_traits_cpu[vec_dot_type].from_float`, applied at 1363/1376. For vec_dot_type = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0 that is `quantize_row_q8_0` (ggml-cpu.c:298) - the RVV routine at arch/riscv/quants.c:32-65. `grep -rn from_float_to_mat ggml/src/ggml-cpu/` returns nothing, so there is no 4-row mat quantizer on the upstream path at all.
findings.finding: The ~490K-cycle scalar quantizer is carried ONLY by baseline / prefetch / d4. The upstream 'before' build quantizes the same 4 activation rows with the vectorized `quantize_row_q8_0`. So the activation path is shared among the three optimized builds but is NOT shared with pristine, and every published prefill speedup is a ratio between a build that pays F and a build that does not.
findings.impact: The bias runs AGAINST the document's own conclusions - the reported speedups are understated, not flattered, so no headline is inflated. But the size is material on small tensors and the document never says so: 4B attn_v d4 is 823,397 cycles of which the fit attributes ~490K to the quantizer; strip the scalar penalty back to gemv's F and the node would be roughly 373K, turning its 10.78x into ~23.8x. A reader takes 'attn_v/attn_k stop at 11.40x' as a property of the kernel or of the tensor shape; it is mostly a property of an unwritten quantizer that only the optimized builds are charged for.

findings.title: The 27B decode figures used in the head-to-head and the absolute-cycles table are not on disk and have no reproduction command
findings.claim_in_doc:
Decode has only five nodes measured at all four stages, so the
head-to-head below uses **those same five on both sides** ... | decode | 2 | 73,356,044 | 36,678,022 |
findings.what_i_checked: `ls sweep-* -d` -> sweep-gemm, sweep-gemm-27b, sweep-gemv (4B only). No sweep-gemv-27b directory exists. sweep.sh line ~68 computes `OUT=$LLAMA/sweep-$MODE$([ "$TAG" = 4b ] || echo "-$TAG")`, so 27B decode logs would live in sweep-gemv-27b/. Ran `MODE=gemv MODEL=27b NODES="53" bash sweep.sh --md` -> all four cells print MISSING. 73,356,044 traces only to profiling_gemv_27b.md:39, not to any log.
findings.finding: Every decode number in this document - the whole right-hand column of the 'Where the prefill speedup comes from' table, the per-layer gemv column, the entire 'Per-node comparison, prefill vs decode' section, and the 73,356,044 cycles that anchor the 'Prefill does twice the tokens in 62% of the cycles' claim - is transcribed from a sibling markdown file whose underlying logs are not present. The 'Reproducing' section gives commands for the 27B prefill legs and for both 4B paths, but none for the 27B decode leg.
findings.impact: Half of every cross-path comparison in the document is unverifiable from the evidence on disk. The prefill-side numbers I could check were all exact, so this is a missing-artifact problem rather than a suspected-error problem, but a third party cannot close the loop on any prefill-vs-decode claim, including the 3.2x-per-token result that the M-tile-sharing story rests on. Needed to clear it: the sweep-gemv-27b/{pristine,baseline,prefetch,d4}-k{48..59}.log set, or a stated command that regenerates it.

findings.title: F=489,581 is quoted to six figures from a fit with +/-5.2% residuals, and the 'bigger than the kernel it feeds' claim flips under a different node pair
findings.claim_in_doc:
Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%) ... at ~490K cycles per node it is the largest
single item in a small prefill matmul -- bigger than the kernel it feeds.
findings.what_i_checked: Re-ran the least-squares fit on the five 4B ne0=2560 nodes from sweep-gemm/*.log and sweep-gemv/*.log. Max relative residual: gemv d4 1.14%, gemm d4 5.19% (per node: attn_q -5.19%, attn_v +4.22%, attn_k +4.23%, ffn_gate +0.46%, ffn_up +0.49%). Also computed every two-point (F, T) solution from the same five points.
findings.finding: The document reports the gemv residual (1.1%) but not the gemm residual, and the headline F comes from the gemm fit, which is roughly five times worse and visibly non-affine - the 16-tile and 64-tile nodes sit on opposite sides of the line. The two-point estimates of gemm-d4 F span 407,238 (attn_q/attn_k) to 689,695 (attn_q/ffn_up), a 1.7x range. Since 4B attn_v d4 totals 823,397 cycles, F = 490K makes the quantizer 59% of the node ('bigger than the kernel it feeds'), while F = 407K makes it 49% - smaller than the kernel. The superlative is an artifact of which pair of nodes the fit weights most.
findings.impact: No speedup table changes; F is unambiguously large and unambiguously dominates the small nodes either way, and my independent ne0-scaling check (27B F ~ 2x 4B F) supports the mechanism. What is not supported is the precision and the superlative: '~490K' should be stated as a range of roughly 0.4M-0.7M, and 'bigger than the kernel it feeds' should be dropped or qualified. Quoting only the better of the two residuals is the presentational problem.

findings.title: The M-tile-sharing citation points at the vd4dots kernel but is used to explain a +repack measurement
findings.claim_in_doc:
Prefill does twice the tokens in 62% of the cycles -- 3.2x cheaper per token --
because the gemm loads each weight vector once and fires four dots against it
(`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`), while the gemv reloads it per token.
findings.what_i_checked: Mapped the function boundaries in arch/riscv/repack.cpp: `#if defined(Q1_VD4DOT) && Q1_VD4DOT` opens at line 1782, `q1_gemm_64_vd4dot_vl1024` spans 1923-1994, the `#else` is at 1996 and `#endif // Q1_VD4DOT` at 2155. build.sh: only the `d4` and `d4-nopf` targets pass `-DGGML_RV_XANDESVDOT=ON`, which is what defines Q1_VD4DOT. The table the sentence explains is explicitly labelled 'On `ffn_gate` at `+repack`'.
findings.finding: Lines 1967-1972 are compiled out of the baseline/prefetch builds. The code that actually produced the cited 45,434,691 and 73,356,044 cycles is `q1_gemm_64x1_vl1024` at lines 2101-2153, where the weight mask is loaded once at line 2121 (`__riscv_vlm_v_b16`) and consumed by four accumulators at 2124-2131. The mechanism claim is true - I verified it in both kernels - but the anchor sends a reader to the wrong build's source.
findings.impact: The conclusion stands unchanged. A reader who checks the citation against a `+repack` build finds those lines preprocessed away and cannot confirm the claim. Fix is a one-line change to cite 2120-2132 (or to cite both, since the shape holds in both).

findings.title: The dispatch gate is quoted as one condition when it has three, plus two outer ones
findings.claim_in_doc:
The dispatch gate at `repack.cpp:4889` requires
`cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0` -- the row-parallel kernel puts 64 rows in 64 vector
lanes -- and both have 48 rows.
findings.what_i_checked: repack.cpp:4885-4891 read in full; `grep -rn 'define QK1_0' ggml/` -> ggml-common.h:180, QK1_0 = 128; repack.cpp:4947-4981 (`supports_op`).
findings.finding: The real gate is `if (__riscv_vlenb() * 8 >= 512 && cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0 && cur->ne[0] % QK1_0 == 0)`, nested inside `cur->type == GGML_TYPE_Q1_0` (4885) and `ggml_cpu_has_riscv_v()` (4886); eligibility is then further filtered by `supports_op` (4947-4959), which additionally requires 2-D src0, src0 living in the repack buffer type, src1 being F32, and src1 residing in a host buffer. The document mentions only the row-count test. For the tensors measured here the omission is harmless - the engine is VLEN 1024 (>= 512), and every ne0 present in either model (2560, 4096, 5120, 6144, 9728, 17408) is a multiple of 128 - so ssm_alpha and ssm_beta really are the only rejects, for exactly the stated reason.
findings.impact: No number or conclusion changes, and the ssm_alpha/ssm_beta diagnosis is correct. The risk is generalization: the closing suggestion 'padding them to 64 rows would bring them in' is only true because ne0=5120 already satisfies the unmentioned ne0 % 128 test, and a reader applying the one-condition rule to another model or another engine (VLEN 256, or a tensor with ne0 not a multiple of 128) would predict eligibility wrongly.

findings.title: The 12.4x fixed-cost gap is attributed entirely to scalar-vs-vector, but 2x of it is simply four tokens instead of two
findings.claim_in_doc:
So decode gets a vector quantizer and prefill gets a scalar one. That is the
whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap
findings.what_i_checked: repack.cpp:4460-4468 - the gemm leg quantizes ne11=4 activation rows, the gemv leg quantizes ne11=2. Fitted gemv d4 F = 39,491 against gemm d4 F = 489,581 from the 4B logs; ratio 12.40x. Sized the vector path: 2 rows x 2560 floats = 5120 elements at 32 f32 lanes (VLEN 1024) is ~160 vector iterations, a small fraction of 39,491.
findings.finding: The two Fs differ in two ways at once, not one: routine (scalar vs RVV) and workload (4 rows vs 2). Even with an identical vector quantizer on both sides, prefill would pay roughly 2x decode. So at most ~6.2x of the 12.4x is attributable to the scalar/vector choice. The residual is also not clean in the other direction: gemv's F = 39,491 is far larger than a 5120-element vectorized quantize can account for, so most of the decode intercept is other per-call overhead (wdata setup, chunking, output store, node dispatch) rather than 'a vector quantizer' - which means F on the gemm side plausibly contains that same overhead too, and is not 100% quantizer either.
findings.impact: Does not change any measured cycle count or speedup. It softens 'That is the whole 12.4x fixed-cost gap' to roughly half of it, and it means the headline 'at ~490K cycles per node' is an upper bound on the quantizer, not an estimate of it. The direction of the argument - vectorize the prefill quantizer, it is the biggest remaining prefill item on small nodes - survives intact.

findings.title: The central causal claim was never measured directly, only inferred from a two-parameter curve fit
findings.claim_in_doc:
`T` collapses 3.5x (gemm) and 6.2x (gemv) as the kernel improves; `F` stays put,
and stays an order of magnitude apart between the two paths. It is the shared
activation path, and the source says what it is.
findings.what_i_checked: Searched the tree and the sibling documents for any direct instrumentation of the quantizer: `grep -n 'quantiz' opt_roadmap.md q1_0_reproduce.md profiling_gemv_27b.md`; inspected the ROI machinery at ggml-cpu.c:1744-1795 (it brackets whole MUL_MAT nodes by graph index only - there is no marker around the quantize loop and no sub-node counter); read build.sh's full target list (pristine / baseline / prefetch / d4 / d4-nopf / *-nodpref) - no variant stubs, replaces or bypasses the activation quantizer.
findings.finding: The identification of F with the scalar quantizer rests entirely on three indirect arguments: F is roughly constant across kernel variants while T collapses, F is ~12x larger on the 4-token path, and the source contains a scalar routine on that path. No profile, no cycle counter around the routine, and no ablation build was run. F is an intercept and therefore absorbs every per-call cost - wdata staging, chunk setup, the dst store, node dispatch - not just the quantizer. To be fair, I built the one cross-check the document omits and it supports the story: fitting the seven 27B ne0=5120 nodes gives F = 824,191 / 920,157 / 895,692 for baseline / prefetch / d4 against 398,003 / 441,355 / 489,581 at 4B's ne0=2560, so F scales with activation length as a per-element quantizer must.
findings.impact: The conclusion is very likely right and I would not dispute it, but 'the source says what it is' oversells inference as demonstration. Two cheap, non-simulation checks would settle it and neither was done: an ROI marker around the 4456-4469 quantize block, or a d4 build whose ggml_quantize_mat_q8_0_4x1_generic body is replaced by a stub (wrong results, but the cycle delta names the cost exactly). Either would convert a 5%-residual curve fit into a measurement.

findings.title: The published layer-7 table cannot be regenerated by the command the document gives for it
findings.claim_in_doc: MODEL=27b NODES="56 57 58 59"             bash sweep.sh --md   # layer 7
findings.what_i_checked: Ran it (safe - `md()` only reads logs and the script exits before the model-file check and before xargs). Output: 4 rows (attn_q, attn_v, attn_k, attn_output) and a total geomean of 15.02x. The published layer-7 table has 7 rows and reports 17.65x.
findings.finding: The three `ffn_*` rows in the layer-7 table are carried from layer 6 by hand and the 17.65x geomean is computed over all seven; the harness cannot produce either. The document does disclose the carry in prose ('Layer 7's three `ffn_*` rows are the same tensor shapes as layer 6's and are carried from them'), so this is a gap between the disclosure and the recipe, not a hidden fabrication - I confirmed 17.65x is the correct 7-value geomean of the printed ratios.

result.summary: Lens 1 reconciles cleanly with one exception. findings.title: Fit quality is reported only for the path where it is good; the gemm d4 fit that produces the headline F has 5.2% residuals
findings.claim_in_doc: Fitting `cycles = F + T * tiles` (gemv residuals within 1.1%):
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:156. Refit all six variant x path pairs by ordinary least squares over the five 4B ne0=2560 nodes and printed per-point residuals. gemv max residual: baseline 0.28%, prefetch 0.11%, d4 1.14% (the "1.1%" claim, right at the edge). gemm max residual: baseline 0.21%, prefetch 0.91%, d4 **5.19%** -- specifically attn_q +5.19%, attn_v -4.22%, attn_k -4.23%, ffn_gate -0.46%, ffn_up -0.49%.
findings.finding: The document reports residual quality for the gemv fits only. The gemm `d4` fit is the worst of the six by a factor of 4.5, and it is the one that yields F = 489,581 -- the number behind "12.4x the per-call fixed cost", "~490K cycles per node", and "F is 59% of 4B attn_v's total". Worse, the largest residuals land precisely on the small nodes (attn_v/attn_k, -4.2%) that the argument is about, so the two-parameter model is least trustworthy exactly where it is being applied. With only three distinct tile counts (16, 64, 152) across five points, the fit is close to determined and cannot distinguish a true constant from mild non-linearity.
findings.impact: Does not overturn the conclusion -- the 12.4x fixed-cost gap between paths is far larger than the residual, and the scalar-quantizer mechanism is independently confirmed in the source (repack.cpp:51 `// scalar`, gated vector twin, -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF in every CMakeCache). But the quoted precision of F (six significant figures) is not supported by a fit with 4-5% residuals, and the reader is given the impression the fit was validated when only half of it was.

findings.title: `--selfcheck` is a file comparison, not the concurrency gate it is advertised as, and its tolerance is 20x the stated noise floor
findings.claim_in_doc: bash sweep.sh --selfcheck     # gate: re-derive two published attn_v numbers
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:256. Read sweep.sh:259-280 and 84-114 before running. run_leg() resumes: if the log already has both a `[roi]` and a cycles line it echoes "have" and returns without launching anything (lines 102-105). Both target logs (sweep-gemm/prefetch-k51.log, sweep-gemm/d4-k51.log, both 2026-08-28) exist, so I ran it: output was `have prefetch k=51` / `have d4 k=51` / `PASS prefetch k=51 1651086 cycles (published 1651949)` / `PASS d4 k=51 823397 cycles (published 818314)`, rc=0, elapsed under a second.
findings.finding: Two things are worth flagging. (1) It is only cheap when the logs are already present -- on a fresh checkout the same command launches two RTL legs, which the doc's Reproducing section lists next to two genuinely free `--md` commands with no warning. (2) In the resumed state it is close to a tautology: it re-reads two files on disk and compares them to two constants hard-coded at sweep.sh:269, so it proves neither that the invocation measures what it claims nor that concurrent hybrid runs do not disturb each other -- both of which sweep.sh:26-29 explicitly claims it proves. Its 1% tolerance (sweep.sh:272) is also loose: the d4 leg passes at 0.62% off its reference, while the document's own stated run-to-run noise floor is 0.05% ("ffn_gate and ffn_up ... agree within 0.05%, which is the run-to-run noise floor here", profiling_gemv_27b.md). A regression of half a percent would pass this gate.
findings.impact: No published number changes. The gate is real when it actually runs a leg, and it did pass. But a reader following the Reproducing section will believe they have validated the harness when in the common case they have validated nothing, and may unintentionally start a simulation.

findings.title: Contradictory figures for the ssm_alpha/ssm_beta weight share (0.12% vs 0.06%)
findings.claim_in_doc: They are 0.06% of the layer's weights but **2.7% of its optimized cycles**

Computed from the doc's own weight column: (245,760 + 245,760) / 383,221,760 = 0.1283%. One tensor alone = 0.0641%. The cycle share checks out: (938,688 + 945,595) / 68,835,932 = 2.74%.

Related minor imprecision at line 69: "their four cycle counts agree to 0.3%" is true of ssm_alpha (936,969..939,798 = 0.30%) but not of ssm_beta (945,595..949,957 = 0.46%).
findings.impact: No conclusion changes -- the point being made (a tiny weight share consuming an outsized cycle share) is if anything understated by the erroneous figure. But two published values for one quantity in one document is a copy-editing failure a reader will notice.

findings.title: The measurement invocation and the build step are under-documented for an outsider
findings.claim_in_doc: | Mode | andesim hybrid, marker trigger, `--no-mmap --mem-size 12G -t 1` |
findings.what_i_checked: profiling_gemm_27b.md:18 against sweep.sh:71-72 and 107-110, and against build.sh. The actual guest invocation is `-m $GGUF --no-mmap -no-cnv --no-warmup --prompt "The capital of France" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1`, with `--step-timeout-ms $TIMEOUT`.
findings.finding: The Setup row names four of the invocation's parameters and omits the ones that decide which kernel is measured: the prompt text and `--no-warmup`. sweep.sh:16-23 is emphatic that the prompt is "the ONLY thing" that selects gemm vs gemv and that getting it wrong "still prints a perfectly plausible cycle count" -- yet the document, which is the artifact a reader will follow, does not state it. Also absent: any mention of build.sh, of the fact that ROI_K is compile-time (build.sh:27-29 explains andesim hands the guest an empty envp, so the node index cannot be an env var), or that 48 separate binaries are needed for the 27B sweep. A reader who runs only the two documented `--md` commands on a fresh checkout gets empty tables, and the only pointer to the fix is a stderr SKIP message inside sweep.sh:97.
findings.impact: Nothing published is wrong. This is the gap between "the tables regenerate" and "an outsider can run the experiment", and it is why the reproducibility grade is (b) rather than (a).

findings.title: Raw logs record almost no provenance
findings.claim_in_doc: Every figure is a cycle-accurate RTL measurement of one MUL_MAT node
findings.what_i_checked: Read sweep-gemm-27b/d4-k57.log in full (22 lines, as are all 48). It contains the staged ELF path (`app=/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/bin-d4-k57`), llama.cpp's system_info line, sampler params, the `[roi]` line and the cycle count.
findings.finding: The logs do record which binary ran, which is the single most useful field and is what let me detect the bin-d4-k59 anomaly. But they record no engine string, no gguf path, no --mem-size, no timestamp, and no llama.cpp build id. Two runs on different engines, different models or different simulator versions produce logs that are identical in every field the harness parses. The engine, the model and the mem-size come from sweep.sh defaults (lines 46-54) and exist only as an untracked file's current contents.
findings.impact: No number is affected. It does mean the logs cannot self-authenticate: the Setup table's engine and model claims rest on the harness defaults, not on the evidence. One cheap fix would be to echo the resolved ENGINE/GGUF/MEM line into each log before the run.

findings.title: The document uses two different files under the same bare name `repack.cpp`
findings.claim_in_doc: The dispatch gate at `repack.cpp:4889` ... (`arch/riscv/repack.cpp:1967-1972`)
findings.what_i_checked: `wc -l` gives ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp = 5009 lines and ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/repack.cpp = 2204 lines. Resolved each citation against both files: 4889, 4456-4469 and 51 are in the generic 5009-line file; 1967-1972 is in the RISC-V one.
findings.finding: Bare `repack.cpp:NNNN` refers to the generic ggml-cpu/repack.cpp while `arch/riscv/repack.cpp:NNNN` refers to the RISC-V one, and both conventions appear in the same document without a note. My first attempt to check `repack.cpp:4889` against the RISC-V file returned nothing (it has only 2204 lines), which reads as a broken citation until you try the other file. Every citation does in fact resolve correctly once disambiguated. Separately, the gate at 4889 has three conjuncts (`__riscv_vlenb() * 8 >= 512 && cur->ne[1] % 64 == 0 && cur->ne[0] % QK1_0 == 0`) and the doc quotes only the row-count one -- accurate for the ssm_alpha/beta explanation, but incomplete as a description of the gate.
findings.impact: None on the numbers. A reader verifying the source claims will hit a false dead end.
